title: Best Encapsulated Crawl Space Dehumidifier (2026): Under-House
h1: The Best Under-House Dehumidifiers for Encapsulated Crawl Spaces
dek: Sealing a crawl space traps the moisture you used to vent away. The right dehumidifier is what turns that liner into a dry, healthy space under your floors.
description: The best dehumidifier for an encapsulated crawl space or under-house space, sized to code, with pumps, Wi-Fi alerts and low-temp defrost for sealed crawls.
intro: Choosing a **dehumidifier for an encapsulated crawl space** is the last, most important step of sealing the space under your house. Encapsulation — a heavy liner over the dirt, closed vents and sealed rim joists — stops ground moisture and humid outdoor air from pouring in. But it also stops the space from breathing. Whatever moisture still sneaks in through the foundation, the plumbing or the house above has nowhere to go, and an **under-house dehumidifier** is the machine that removes it.

That makes this a different purchase from a general crawl-space unit. In a sealed crawl you're controlling a fixed volume of air, so efficiency, a precise humidistat and code-compliant sizing matter more than brute force. You also need a unit that drains without harming the liner, survives cool spring temperatures and tells you when something goes wrong.
Below are five under-house dehumidifiers built for sealed crawls, plus the code math, liner details and setup advice that separate a dry crawl from an expensive science project.

blocks.text: Recent editions of the International Residential Code allow several ways to condition an unvented crawl: a dehumidifier, a small continuous exhaust fan or a supply duct from the HVAC system. In humid climates most homeowners choose the dehumidifier because it controls humidity directly. Your jurisdiction may use an older code, so confirm what your inspector expects.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for encapsulated crawl spaces

blocks.text: We don't run a lab or install units for review. We compared manufacturer ratings — AHAM capacity, sealed-space coverage, minimum operating temperature and ENERGY STAR status — plus manuals for drainage, ducting and hanging options. We checked CPSC recalls and read owner reviews from people with sealed crawls, watching for failed pumps, iced coils and noisy compressors.

We weighted efficiency and code-friendly capacity highest, since a sealed crawl's dehumidifier runs for much of the year, then self-draining options, remote alerts and a footprint that fits real crawl clearances.

items.label: Capacity that meets your code
items.text: Multiply your crawl's floor area by 0.07 to get the pints-per-day figure recent codes call for. Compare that against AHAM ratings, not the bigger saturation number.

items.text: Gravity to daylight or a sump, or a pump. Never let condensate run onto the vapor barrier. Our [crawl space dehumidifier installation](/guides/crawl-space-dehumidifier-installation/) guide covers each route.

sections.heading: What size dehumidifier for an encapsulated crawl space?

blocks.text: There are two ways to size a sealed crawl, and they don't always agree. Manufacturers rate units by the area they can keep dry in a tight space — the Compact70 and E070 both list about 2,200 square feet. Recent residential codes are stricter: 70 pints a day for every 1,000 square feet of crawl floor.

blocks.caption: Code requirements vary by jurisdiction and edition. Where code doesn't apply, the maker's sealed-space rating is a reasonable guide.

blocks.text: For permitted work, size to the code figure. For an existing encapsulation, the maker's rating is usually fine if the liner is continuous and the vents are truly sealed. Big crawls under a humid house may be better served by a ducted unit from our [whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) picks.

sections.heading: Sealed vs. vented: does a crawl space need encapsulation first?

blocks.text: Vented crawl spaces were designed to dry by trading air with the outdoors. In humid summers that backfires: warm, wet air flows in, meets cool joists and ductwork, and condenses. A dehumidifier in that space is trying to dry the neighborhood, so it runs constantly and still loses on muggy days.
Can you use a dehumidifier in a crawl space without encapsulation?

You can, but expect weak results unless you at least close the vents and cover the soil. A 6-mil polyethylene ground cover and sealed vents capture much of the benefit for a fraction of the cost. These are the encapsulation steps that matter most to the dehumidifier:

items: **Fix bulk water.** Gutters, downspouts and grading first. A dehumidifier can't keep up with liquid water.
**Lay a continuous vapor retarder.** Codes call for at least a Class I retarder (6-mil poly is the usual minimum); contractors often use tougher 10–20 mil reinforced liners.
**Overlap and tape seams.** Six inches of overlap, taped, with the liner running at least 6 inches up the wall and fastened there.
**Seal vents, rim joists and penetrations,** including gaps around pipes, wires and the access door.
**Then add the dehumidifier.** Set it off the liner, level it and start at 50–55%.

sections.heading: How much does an under-house dehumidifier cost?

blocks.text: Expect to pay from several hundred dollars for a compact gravity-drain unit to $2,000 or more for a 70- to 90-pint pro model. A condensate pump, drain line and blocks add a little if you install it yourself; contractor installation of the dehumidifier alone usually lands around $1,500–$3,000 total. Full encapsulation with a dehumidifier is the big ticket, commonly $5,000–$15,000 or more depending on size and condition. Because a sealed-crawl unit cycles for much of the year, efficiency ratings carry real weight in the long-run cost.

sections.heading: Setting up a dehumidifier after encapsulation

items: **Find the middle.** Place the unit centrally, or near the hatch with a duct running to the far end of a long crawl.
**Keep it off the liner.** Use blocks, a platform or a manufacturer-approved hanging kit. Our [best hanging dehumidifier](/best/best-hanging-dehumidifier/) guide covers suspended installs.
**Use a GFCI outlet.** Crawl-space receptacles need GFCI protection; skip extension cords.
**Give it a week.** A freshly sealed crawl can take several days to come down from the 70s into the 50s; after that, expect short cycles.

blocks.text: Encapsulation keeps water out; the dehumidifier keeps the air in check. The **Santa Fe Compact70** is the best all-round under-house dehumidifier for a sealed crawl, combining 70 pints with top-tier efficiency in a hatch-friendly body. faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for an encapsulated crawl space?
faqs.a: For most sealed crawls, the Santa Fe Compact70: 70 pints a day, rated for sealed spaces up to about 2,200 square feet, with ENERGY STAR Most Efficient recognition. Choose the Aprilaire E070W for Wi-Fi alerts or the AlorAir HDi65S for a built-in pump.

faqs.q: Does an encapsulated crawl space need a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: In most climates, yes. Sealing the crawl stops outdoor air from drying it, so moisture from the foundation, plumbing and house above needs another way out. Codes accept a dehumidifier, a small exhaust fan or conditioned supply air; in humid regions, a dehumidifier gives the most reliable control.

faqs.q: Should I put a dehumidifier in a crawl space without encapsulation?
faqs.a: It's usually a poor use of money. In a vented crawl with bare soil, the unit dries outdoor air and the ground and rarely reaches its target. Cover the soil and seal the vents first.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for an under-house crawl space?
faqs.a: Recent residential codes call for 70 pints a day per 1,000 square feet of crawl floor. Manufacturer ratings are more generous for tightly sealed spaces, often about 2,200 square feet for a 70-pint unit. Follow code for permitted work.

faqs.q: How much does an under-house dehumidifier cost?
faqs.a: The unit runs from several hundred dollars to $2,000 or more. Professional installation of the dehumidifier usually totals about $1,500–$3,000, while full encapsulation with a dehumidifier often costs $5,000–$15,000 or more.

faqs.q: What humidity should an encapsulated crawl space be?
faqs.a: Most installers set sealed crawls to about 50–55% relative humidity. Readings that stay above 60% for days point to a leak, a gap in the liner or an undersized or failing unit.
